Treatment of Possible PERM Underlying Malignant Catatonia and Accompanying Psychotic Symptoms With Modified Electroconvulsive Therapy: A Case Report
A 47-year-old woman
Department of Psychiatry, Osaka General Medical Center, Osaka, Japan
A 47-year-old woman
A 47-year-old woman with normal intelligence experienced difficulty with walking, and developed incontinence, incoherence, and soliloquy within a month.
She was discharged 127 days after hospitalization, with followups on an outpatient basis. At 118 days after discharge from the hospital, no complications related to ECT were observed.

extractions.value: Patient diagnosed with possible PERM underlying malignant catatonia. Seronegative PERM with no evidence of malignancy. mECT administered on days 43, 45, 50, 52 of hospitalization; 8 mECT treatments total. Discharged 127 days after hospitalization. At 118 days after discharge, mRS score 1, with residual spastic gait and difficulty walking down stairs.
extractions.quote: The patient was diagnosed with possible PERM underlying malignant catatonia... She was treated with mECT on days 43, 45, 50, and 52 of hospitalization... Immobility, hyperreflexia, urinary incontinence, muteness, and dysphagia disappeared after 8 mECT treatments... She was discharged 127 days after hospitalization... At 118 days after discharge from the hospital... the patient had difficulties in walking down the stairs owing to spastic gait... (mRS score, 1).
